image.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: professional hairstyle-analysis teaching image for a mobile training app
Primary request: Create a realistic 2-by-2 contact sheet documenting the CURRENT hairstyle and body proportions of one fictional adult East Asian woman from four fully consistent views: front, exact right profile, exact left profile, and exact back. This is one current-condition record for analysing whether a jaw-length geometric box bob from a reference can be adapted to her; it is not a makeover, not a before/after comparison, and must not show the reference hairstyle or any proposed result.

Scene/backdrop: identical plain warm light-gray studio background in every panel; no salon tools, mirror, chair, props, extra people, text or labels.
Subject: the exact same fictional woman in every panel, early-to-mid 30s, natural unretouched skin, neutral relaxed expression, ordinary realistic appearance. Dark natural brown hair with medium-to-high visible density and medium-to-coarse-looking strands. Current haircut is a straight collarbone-length lob with a continuous slightly heavy baseline resting just above and lightly touching the shoulders, low-to-mid visual weight, modest root lift, softly off-center natural part, no short bangs, long face-framing pieces that can tuck behind the ears. Most of the hair looks straight, while the inner nape and very ends show a subtle irregular inward/outward bend from natural growth and shoulder contact. Temple areas should look slightly less full than the back, but not balding or medically abnormal. Hair is clean and naturally blow-dried, not flat-ironed, not wet, not glossy slick.
Proportions for teaching: full shoulders visibly somewhat broad relative to the head silhouette; neck of medium length; head and face proportions natural and consistent. Do not exaggerate or beautify. The current lower hair width should sit near the collarbone/shoulder area, leaving the upper sides comparatively quiet.
Body/framing: full head, complete hairstyle outline and baseline, both ears as naturally appropriate to each angle, entire neck, both shoulders and upper chest visible in every panel. Neutral level head and posture; no tilt. On the front view the hair remains down rather than tucked so the current outline is readable.
Clothing: identical simple matte muted slate-blue wide crew-neck top in all panels, no collar, jewelry or accessories, so neck and shoulder proportions stay visible.
Style/medium: honest photorealistic studio reference photography, realistic individual strands, flyaways, pores and everyday texture; no beauty filter, glamour retouching or face reshaping.
Composition/layout: landscape 2-by-2 contact sheet with four equal panels and narrow neutral gutters. Top-left front, top-right exact right profile, bottom-left exact left profile, bottom-right exact back. Same camera height, subject scale, focal length, crop, shoulder level and soft diffused daylight in all panels.
Output intent: current-condition evidence for advanced hairstylist training about adapting a geometric jaw-length reference to head/shoulder proportions, temple density, mixed straight-and-bent texture, ear-tuck function and low-maintenance styling.
Constraints/invariants: same identity, face, head, neck and shoulder proportions, clothing, current haircut length, density pattern, bend pattern and lighting in all four panels. Only one adult person repeated across views. Show only the current collarbone lob. No reference image, no haircut result, no geometric jaw bob, no before/after, no comparison hairstyle, no salon finish. No labels, text, arrows or watermark.
Avoid: short bob result, micro bangs, heavy fringe, dramatic layers, strong curls, wet look, severe asymmetry, shaved areas, polished advertising hair, hidden neck, cropped shoulders, three-quarter angles substituted for true profiles, inconsistent identity or hair length, duplicated front views, dramatic makeup, medical-looking hair loss.
